dependency_simplification:
DRIFT / REUSE
Searched pinned mathlib TuringMachine/Tape, ToPartrec and StackTuringMachine,
original Transpose/Tape, local marked-copy and scheduled action/motion
modules. Mathlib supplies Tape.move_left_nth, Tape.move_right_nth,
Tape.move_right_n_head and Tape.write_nth; these underlie the existing
absolute-tape/native cell-action interface, which is reused. ToPartrec's
copy_ok proves qualitative TM2 reachability using reversed stack lists;
it does not supply this native two-tape, exact-clock and all-prefix head
path interface. The local NativeMappedCopy handles marked words; its
cell-action foundation is reused, while the new transfer handles exact
public lengths on a live shared bank. This is a targeted reuse search,
not a claim that no equivalent theorem exists anywhere.
All finite schedule composition uses existing append_exact/append_active
and append_position. Rewinds reuse ScheduledTapeAction. All affine covers
and rounding reuse clippedRamp_cover/sample_error and the existing .add
and .sub closure results. No duplicate compactness, native compiler,
normalization or asymptotic state-bit proof was introduced.
The new operation fills an explicit source206 palette requirement and
provides the concrete building block for backward masked scans and paid
rotation. Do not turn this into another stand-alone reversal impossibility
proof; next integrate the remaining operations with the existing shared-
bank word compiler, then complete the mixed-word exclusion. The row,
integer and F3 palettes remain real obligations, not informal corollaries.
novelty: No novelty claim. A concrete required internal stage is now proved, not an additional unrestricted transposition theorem.
